interest: This file offers historians a unique composite index of how the U.S. State Department monitored, responded to, and memorialized prominent Japanese figures during a pivotal decade defined by mounting political violence and delicate international relations. It vividly illustrates the internal crisis of early 1930s Japan through the clustered assassinations of moderate civilian leaders—such as Finance Minister Inouye, Mitsui chief Baron Dan, and Premier Inukai—by ultranationalist and militarist groups. At the same time, the extensive correspondence concerning Viscount Shibusawa's biographical project and Admiral Togo's state funeral highlights subtle nuances of diplomatic protocol, inter-service and international rivalries over ceremonial representation, and unexpected public relations friction like NBC's broadcasting faux pas. Furthermore, as a purport sheet file, it provides an invaluable archival roadmap to decimal file 894.44 and related cross-references across general political records, naval files, and biographical dossiers.
keywords: Special Mention of Subjects of Japan
overview: This file comprises docket sheets (purport lists and jacket case lists of papers) for decimal file 894.44 ('Special Mention of Citizens or Subjects of Japan Not Otherwise Classifiable') in the U.S. State Department's central records from 1930 to 1939. Rather than preserving original despatches and diplomatic notes, these sheets catalogue and index incoming and outgoing correspondence, memoranda, telegrams, and cross-reference entries concerning prominent Japanese statesmen, military figures, diplomats, jurists, and industrialists. Major sections track the political violence of 1932, including the assassinations of Prime Minister Ki Inukai, Finance Minister Junnosuke Inouye, and Mitsui leader Baron Takuma Dan, as well as the death of General Yoshinori Shirakawa from wounds sustained in the Shanghai Hongkew bombing. Other sections record condolence exchanges, protocol arrangements, and commemorations following the deaths of former Prime Minister Yuko Hamaguchi, former Ambassador Masanao Hanihara, industrialist Viscount Eiichi Shibusawa, and Admiral Marquis Heihachiro Togo, alongside inquiries regarding legal treatises and diplomatic memoirs by scholars and diplomats such as Viscount Kikujiro Ishii and Dr. Sakutaro Tachi.

subfiles.about: Docket list recording State Department correspondence and internal memoranda concerning various prominent Japanese subjects, scholars, publications, and political leaders.
subfiles.summary: This docket sheet tracks sub-numbers 16 through 24 of decimal file 894.44 between December 1935 and May 1939. It notes an article by Foreign Minister Koki Hirota in Hinode recounting his diplomatic career and memories of Yamaza Ejiro, as well as inquiries by James Grafton Rogers and Whitney Griswold regarding Sakutaro Tachi's book on international law. It further catalogues internal State Department memoranda assessing prominent Japanese women, biographical sketches of Yosuke Matsuoka, and political commentary on Marquis Koichi Kido as a candidate for Prime Minister.
subfiles.title: List of Papers on Special Mention of Subjects of Japan (General)

subfiles.about: Docket list indexing diplomatic reporting and cross-references regarding the assassination of Mitsui Director-General Baron Takuma Dan.
subfiles.summary: This jacket case list catalogues four records from March and April 1932 concerning the murder of Baron Takuma Dan outside the Mitsui Bank in Tokyo. It details telegrams and despatches from Ambassador W. Cameron Forbes and Chargé Edwin L. Neville reporting the arrest of assassin Goro Hishinuma of Ibaraki Prefecture. Subsequent entries link the assassination to the ultranationalist Blood Brotherhood League and record cross-references to the embassy's political reports.
subfiles.title: List of Papers on the Assassination of Baron Takuma Dan

subfiles.about: Docket sheet tracking condolences and messages of gratitude exchanged following the death of former Prime Minister Yuko Hamaguchi.
subfiles.summary: This docket sheet records three communications from late August 1931 relating to the death of former Japanese Prime Minister Yuko Hamaguchi. It details the transmission of official American condolences to the Hamaguchi family via Foreign Minister Baron Kijuro Shidehara. It also logs telegraphic acknowledgments and expressions of thanks returned by both Shidehara and the Hamaguchi family.
subfiles.title: List of Papers on the Death of Former Premier Yuko Hamaguchi

subfiles.about: Docket sheet listing diplomatic correspondence and personal messages of condolence on the death of former Ambassador Masanao Hanihara.
subfiles.summary: This jacket case sheet catalogues seven communications from December 1934 concerning the death of former Japanese Ambassador to the United States Masanao Hanihara. It records Ambassador Joseph C. Grew's arrangements to attend the funeral in Tokyo and send an official embassy wreath. It also tracks personal condolences conveyed to Hanihara's widow by Under Secretary William Phillips and Major General Frank McCoy, an old associate.
subfiles.title: List of Papers on the Death of Former Ambassador Masanao Hanihara

subfiles.about: Docket sheet indexing diplomatic reporting on the assassination of former Minister of Finance Junnosuke Inouye.
subfiles.summary: This docket sheet records a single entry for despatch No. 517 of March 10, 1932, submitted by Ambassador W. Cameron Forbes in Tokyo. The despatch reports on the assassination of Junnosuke Inouye, an outstanding Minseito leader who served twice as Japanese Minister of Finance. The entry cross-references comprehensive reporting on the murder filed under decimal number 894.00 P.R./51.
subfiles.title: List of Papers on the Assassination of Junnosuke Inouye

subfiles.about: Docket sheet summarising diplomatic despatches, international press commentary, and official findings concerning the May 15, 1932 assassination of Prime Minister Ki Inukai.
subfiles.summary: This list of papers indexes six communications from May 1932 to June 1933 regarding the assassination of Prime Minister Ki Inukai during the May 15 Incident. It catalogues reporting by Edwin L. Neville on the causes, political results, and public repercussions of the attack, as well as German press reactions forwarded from Berlin and condolences from American residents in Chosen (Seoul). The final entry notes Ambassador Grew's report on the lifting of official press censorship and the release of the Japanese government's formal investigation findings.
subfiles.title: List of Papers on the Assassination of Prime Minister Ki Inukai

subfiles.about: Docket sheet cataloguing correspondence and translation inquiries regarding Viscount Kikujiro Ishii's diplomatic memoirs 'Gaiko Yoron'.
subfiles.summary: This jacket case sheet tracks eight documents from 1930 and 1931 concerning the publication of Viscount Kikujiro Ishii's memoirs, entitled 'Gaiko Yoron' (A Review of Foreign Relations / Diplomatic Commentaries). It notes Embassy Tokyo's transmission of Japanese press reviews, State Department authorization to purchase a copy, and a translation of the table of contents prepared by Consul William R. Langdon. It also catalogues inquiries from Professor Robert J. Kerner of the University of California regarding translation rights and progress.
subfiles.title: List of Papers on Viscount Kikujiro Ishii's Memoirs

subfiles.about: Docket sheet recording a briefing memorandum prepared for the Secretary of State prior to a call by Japanese industrialist Masao Shibusawa.
subfiles.summary: This list of papers contains a single entry from October 13, 1931, recording a biographical sketch of Masao Shibusawa prepared by Turner of the Far Eastern Division. The memorandum was addressed to the Secretary of State for use during Shibusawa's scheduled diplomatic call on October 19. It notes that the prominent industrialist was to be accompanied to the meeting by the Counselor of the Japanese Embassy.
subfiles.title: List of Papers on Masao Shibusawa

subfiles.about: Three-page docket list cataloguing condolence messages upon the death of Viscount Eiichi Shibusawa, memorials submitted to President Hoover, and diplomatic efforts to obtain American presidential photographs for his official biography.
subfiles.summary: This three-page docket list indexes 35 sub-numbers from November 1931 to November 1937 concerning Viscount Eiichi Shibusawa. The initial pages track condolences conveyed by the U.S. Government, former Ambassador Charles MacVeagh, and the Spokane Chamber of Commerce following Shibusawa's death in November 1931, as well as memorial items presented to President Herbert Hoover by Dr. Kyugoro Obata. The latter two pages record extensive correspondence in 1936 and 1937 between Embassy Tokyo, the State Department, the National Archives, the Library of Congress, and industrialist James A. Farrell to procure and forward photographs of Presidents Grant, Theodore Roosevelt, and Taft, as well as Judge Elbert H. Gary, for inclusion in Shibusawa's published biography.
subfiles.title: List of Papers on Viscount Eiichi Shibusawa (Pages 1-3)

subfiles.about: Docket sheet tracking consular and diplomatic reports on the death of General Baron Yoshinori Shirakawa following the Hongkew Park bombing.
subfiles.summary: This list of papers indexes two records from May and June 1932 regarding General Baron Yoshinori Shirakawa. It catalogues a telegram from Consul General Edwin S. Cunningham in Shanghai reporting Shirakawa's death from wounds suffered in the Hongkew Park bombing incident. A subsequent despatch from Edwin L. Neville in Tokyo provides further details and cross-references substantive political reporting filed under 894.00 P.R./54.
subfiles.title: List of Papers on the Death of General Baron Yoshinori Shirakawa

subfiles.about: Three-page docket list detailing diplomatic correspondence, naval representation, protocol determinations, and broadcasting controversies concerning the state funeral of Admiral Marquis Heihachiro Togo.
subfiles.summary: This three-page docket sheet indexes 25 entries from May to July 1934 concerning the death and state funeral of Admiral Marquis Heihachiro Togo. It records official American messages of condolence, the dispatch of Admiral Frank B. Upham aboard the flagship USS Augusta to Yokohama to represent the U.S. Navy, and discussions regarding Ambassador Grew's formal designation as personal representative of the President. The concluding entries document Japanese expressions of gratitude alongside diplomatic reports on domestic Japanese irritation caused by a radio broadcasting faux pas committed by the National Broadcasting Company (NBC) during the funeral ceremonies.
subfiles.title: List of Papers on the Death and State Funeral of Admiral Marquis Heihachiro Togo (Pages 1-3)
